R0175.title: Blockchain Replay Attack
R0175.definition: Attackers replay a legitimate transaction from one chain on another chain or the same chain, causing assets to be transferred repeatedly.
R0175.description: In blockchain fork or cross-chain scenarios, if transaction signatures do not include chain ID or other replay protection identifiers, attackers can copy a user's signed transaction from one chain and execute it on another. Typical scenarios include two chains after a hard fork, cross-chain transfers, contract upgrades, etc. Users may unknowingly lose assets on multiple chains.
R0175.influence: User assets are repeatedly transferred on multiple chains, causing additional losses.

observables: The same signed transaction is executed on both chains after a fork, with assets transferred repeatedly
In cross-chain transfer scenarios, the transaction signature lacks replay protection identifiers such as a chain ID
A user's authorization signature on one chain is copied and replayed on another chain, causing unintended asset transfers
After a contract upgrade or fork, old signatures remain validly executable on the new chain
